Bring two spatial objects to one CRS

Source: R/crs-geometry.R
harmonize_crs.Rd

Brings two sf or sfc objects to one CRS: the CRS of a or b, as prefer says, or target_crs when it is given. Without target_crs, two objects that both lack a CRS are returned unchanged.

Usage

harmonize_crs(
  a,
  b,
  prefer = c("a", "b"),
  target_crs = NULL,
  on_transform_error = c("stop", "set_crs")
)

Arguments

a, b

Objects of class sf or sfc.

prefer

Which object's CRS both are brought to when they differ: "a" (default) or "b". Ignored when target_crs is given.

target_crs

Optional target CRS to apply to both: anything sf::st_crs() accepts, including an sf or sfc object, whose CRS is used.

on_transform_error

What to do when sf::st_transform() fails: "stop" (default) raises an error; "set_crs" relabels the CRS with sf::st_set_crs() without moving the coordinates. Use "set_crs" only when the coordinates are already in the target CRS.

Value

A named list with components a and b, each of the class it came in. A layer that is not transformed is returned as it came.

Details

When one input has no CRS, the lon/lat test that ensure_projected() uses decides what happens (see spatialkit-geometry, "Layers without a CRS"), so both functions place the same data in the same place: coordinates the test takes for degrees are read as EPSG:4326 and reprojected to the other object's CRS (or target_crs); other coordinates are stamped with that CRS by sf::st_set_crs(), which relabels them without moving them. Either way a warning says so. A CRS in longitude and latitude is not stamped on coordinates that cannot be in it: a layer with an x outside -180 to 360 or a y beyond 90 north or south, read on the coordinates that have a location, stops the call with an error that names a or b, its box and the target CRS.

A layer that is transformed is read as spatialkit-geometry describes: a layer that mixes XY and XYZ (or XYM) geometries comes back in XY, with a warning of class spatialkit_zm_dropped, and a row without a location comes back empty, in its own geometry type. So does a row of a projected layer moved to a CRS in degrees with a coordinate beyond 1e10 in its CRS's own unit, further out than any projected CRS places a point of the Earth. A row that has a location and that the target CRS cannot place in full, such as a point far outside a UTM zone or a ring with a vertex at a latitude beyond 90, comes back empty, or without the vertices the CRS cannot place, and a warning of class spatialkit_rows_unplaced names such rows of a or b (rows on the condition).

See also

spatialkit-geometry for how input geometry and CRSs are read.

Other data preparation: [.spatialkit_rows(), coerce_to_points(), ensure_projected(), prep_model_data(), spatialkit-geometry

Examples

library(sf)
a <- st_as_sf(data.frame(x = c(500000, 500100), y = c(4000000, 4000100)),
              coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632)
b <- st_transform(a, 4326)                 # same points, lon/lat
h <- harmonize_crs(a, b)                    # b is brought into a's CRS
c(a = st_crs(h$a)$epsg, b = st_crs(h$b)$epsg)
#>     a     b 
#> 32632 32632 
st_crs(h$a) == st_crs(h$b)
#> [1] TRUE
